text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- ENERGY SECTOR NEEDS $6 BILLION IN INVESTMENTS
Brazil's energy sector needs to invest around $6 billion over the next three years if power cuts and rationing are to be avoided, according to a Paribas analyst.
-- GENCOR WANTS INFLUENTIAL POSITION IN CVRD
South African mining company Gencor is looking to gain an influential stake of at least 10 percent in a consortium which will participate in the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD.
-- EVEN TELERJ POSTS PROFIT IN 1996
Brazil's five main state telephone operators posted significant profit gains in 1996, with Rio de Janeiro state's telephone company Telerj announcing the first profit in five years.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PRIVATIZED STATE FIRMS HAVE CUT JOBS 33 PERCENT
State firms which have been privatized since 1991 have cut some 39,631 jobs or 32.6 percent of total jobs since they were sold off.
-- CPI WANTS CENBANK DISMISSALS
A special Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) wants to see the dismissal of Central Bank officials who are linked to the emmission of apparently illegal state and city bonds.
O GLOBO
-- MORE DETAILED CPI INVESTIGATION DIVIDES SENATE

The Brazilian Senate is divided over whether to authorize a special Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) to expand its investigations into a multi-million-dollar scam involving state and city bonds to the country's entire banking sector.
-- DEVELOPMENT BANK MAY FUND SHANTYTOWN PROJECT
The Interamerican Development Bank is studying the possibility to help fund a project improving Rio de Janeiro's shantytowns.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
